summary: Steel Aermotor fire tower in Iron County's Riverside Conservation Area; a 2018-2019 MDC infrastructure assessment recommended removal, and its current state is unconfirmed.

facts.design: Aermotor galvanized steel tower with a pyramid-roofed cab, similar to the LS-40 or MC-39 designs
facts.status_note: A survey report from about 2019 says the tower is slated for demolition; no source I could read confirms its current state.

access.note: The base is enclosed by a chain-link fence topped with barbed wire.

events.note: Land bought for the fire tower site, mainly for wildfire prevention
Temporary wooden tower, 52 ft; the sources differ on its type and dates
Temporary wooden tower dismantled, per the report
Steel Aermotor tower erected; the report gives 1955-56 and notes maps show a tower by 1954
Other site buildings removed; the tower was kept
Radio repeater added; new role as an emergency radio receiving site
Infrastructure assessment (2018-2019) recommended removal; a report recommended the tower as eligible for the National Register

corrections.why: 15.8 m (52 ft) is the earlier wooden tower; the steel tower on the site is 60 ft (18.3 m) per the report
The report says MDC owns and maintains the tower; the commission was the agency's earlier name when it bought the land in 1939

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The annual-report summary says a temporary pole tower in 1939-41 and a 52-ft wooden tower in 1943; the report says a temporary wood tower in 1943, dismantled in 1954. For the steel tower, the reports give 1955-56 but maps show a tower by 1954. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Current status is unknown. A GovDeals surplus listing (https://www.govdeals.com/en/asset/2407/10178) appeared in search with a removal window of 1 Nov 2023 to 15 Mar 2024. GovDeals returns 403 to our fetcher, so it is not cited, and the search snippet was not checked against the page. Its asset numbers match the PDF's file path (10178, 2407). Check whether the tower was removed before publishing. The PDF shows no title, author or date on the extract; the 2019 personal-communication citations suggest about 2019-2020. The record's 52 ft height describes the earlier wooden tower. The NHLR Missouri list (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/MO) does not include Vulcan.
